root_cause_label: No KV buffer for multi-position attention and misidentified repetitive garbage output as success
one_sentence_failure_summary: The agent implemented a transformer with no key-value cache across positions (every token attends only to itself), making autoregressive inference architecturally impossible, and then at step 55 misidentified the resulting prompt-invariant repetitive output as a working solution.
t_err_evidence: In step 9, the compact rewrite encodes the decisive architectural flaw: the transformer function receives a single embedding vector x and position p but has no stored buffer of previous K and V vectors; all attention 'history' pointers (k, v) point into the same current-token QKV array, so attention over positions 0..p always uses the same key/value data regardless of which prior token was processed.
t_commit_evidence: At step 55, after the program first produces legible text tokens ('essionsessions...'), the agent declares 'Great progress! The model is now producing actual text output' and 'The model is working', deciding the task is essentially done despite the output being prompt-invariant and repetitive. From this point all subsequent steps are either superficial re-checks or minor attention-indexing changes that do not address the architectural flaw.
t_surface_evidence: Step 19 terminal output shows './a.out gpt2-124M.ckpt vocab.bpe "The"' producing 'ersersersersersersersersersersersersersersersersersersersers' — a clearly repetitive, degenerate output indicating the model is not functioning correctly.
trigger_explanation: The agent lacks the domain knowledge that autoregressive GPT-2 inference requires a key-value cache: each generation step must attend over all prior positions' cached K and V vectors. The agent's transformer function operates on a single embedding vector without any persistent KV buffer, so it can only compute self-attention on the single current token, making the sequence position argument meaningless.
forewarning_evidence: Steps 19, 24, 37, 41, 48, 51 all show degenerate repetitive outputs ('ersers', 'KKKK', '0000') that are identical or near-identical across different prompts. Steps 57-58 explicitly show 'Hello' and 'Machine' produce the identical token sequence as 'The', which the agent notes but continues past.
